Filippo Brunelleschi. The Florentine architect and engineer who pioneered Renaissance architecture and linear perspective, creating one of history's greatest architectural triumphs.

Brunelleschi lived from 1377 to 1446. His most famous achievement is the massive dome of Florence Cathedral, which he designed and constructed beginning in 1420. This was a feat of engineering without interior scaffolding that became one of history's greatest architectural achievements. The dome employed a double-shell structure and herringbone brick pattern, combining structural necessity with geometric beauty. No precedent existed for such a span.

He invented or perfected linear perspective, the mathematical system for representing three-dimensional space on a flat surface, revolutionizing both architecture and painting. He designed the Basilica of San Lorenzo in Florence, establishing the principles of Renaissance proportion and harmonic design based on geometric ratios. He created the Pazzi Chapel, a small chapel embodying symmetry, classical orders, and harmonious proportions that defined early Renaissance aesthetics.

Brunelleschi studied in Rome, measuring classical ruins and integrating Roman architectural principles—columns, entablatures, and proportional systems—into Renaissance design. He recognized that buildings should integrate mathematical precision with artistic vision.

He is recognized as the first major architect of the Renaissance, bridging medieval Gothic with classical revival and establishing Florence as the artistic center of Europe. Later Florentine geniuses like Leonardo da Vinci would follow in combining mathematical precision with artistic vision as Brunelleschi had pioneered. Florence Cathedral itself became his masterpiece, and the dome defines both Florence and Renaissance achievement. Brunelleschi's work launched the cultural and architectural movement that would define an age.
